study: GR00T N1.5 fp16 TensorRT engines timed standalone (trtexec-style, batch 1): ViT, LLM, one DiT denoise step
accounting: stage_sum = ViT + LLM + 4 x DiT_step (4 denoise steps). Excludes the small action-head graphs, transforms and host glue -- see the full-pipeline e2e records for the whole policy call.

vs_nvidia_published.source: SOURCED: NVIDIA Isaac-GR00T N1.5 deployment_scripts/README.md (trtexec, batch_size=1)

orin_valid_comparison.note: same TensorRT major version (10.3) as NVIDIA's table
orin_valid_comparison.reading: agreement to 0.5% in total, with per-stage deltas mixed in sign -- consistent with identical work measured identically (theirs with jetson_clocks on, ours off)

thor_not_a_validation.note: TensorRT versions differ (ours 10.16.2 vs NVIDIA's older table), so the -10% is version drift, not a harness advantage. Recorded, not claimed.

fp16_build_trap.what: Building the Qwen3 LLM engine with plain --fp16 (not strongly typed) prints PASSED and produces plausible values while being structurally wrong (cosine ~0.853, rel_mae ~0.65 vs the ONNX reference) on all three GPUs.
fp16_build_trap.detector: a correct build keeps the RMSNorm fp32 regions (98 Float tensors in the engine's layer info); a broken build has zero.
fp16_build_trap.consequence: speed/build_engines.py builds STRONGLY TYPED networks; do not switch it to --fp16.

thor_dit_note: Thor's DiT step (4.94 ms) is about as slow as its own ViT and only 1.64x faster than Orin's (ViT 2.53x, LLM 2.05x); three independent builds agree to 0.48% and the engine is numerically correct (cosine 0.99999). A first-order roofline places the DiT below Thor's ridge, i.e. memory-bandwidth-bound (DERIVED, not measured here).
harness: speed/e2e_eager_hybrid_fulltrt.py (standalone_engine_ms) reproduces these per-engine times in the same session as the e2e runs
